intended_object: The graded module map S_i → (soc P_i){−2} given by right multiplication by the volume element vol_i = (i→j→i). Here P_i = Z e_i is the indecomposable projective of the zigzag algebra Z of a finite graph without isolated vertices, and S_i is its graded simple head. The map raises internal degree by two and gives the head–socle isomorphism S_i{2} ≅ soc P_i (Huerfano–Khovanov §3, Ehrig–Tubbenhauer Prop. 2.8). This is read off from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The body defines the map on the quotient presentation of S_i, the quotient of Z e_i by the positive-degree part. The map is x ↦ x · vol_i. It is well defined because the positive-degree ideal kills vol_i: in the zigzag algebra every element of degree ≥ 3 is zero (`positiveIdeal_smul_socleVolume`). The target is the socle, realized as Z e_i ∩ J². That description is correct when there are no isolated vertices, which is why the hypothesis `hns` is assumed, and the file proves it against Mathlib's `socle` (`socle_zigzagProjective_eq_comap`). The grading also checks out. S_i sits in degree 0 and vol_i in degree 2. The piece of degree p of `shiftObj (-2)` is the piece of degree p+2 of the original module, so the map is homogeneous of degree 0 into the shifted socle, i.e. it raises internal degree by two, as the docstring says. `zigzagGradedHeadToSocle_mk` confirms the map is right multiplication by the volume, and the library proves it is an isomorphism, as the references state. This is a specific morphism attached to zigzag algebras: its content needs that setting, and Mathlib has no general counterpart. So it is not too narrow; it works over any field k for any finite graph without isolated vertices.
